skill.name: adaptyv
skill.description: Use Adaptyv to plan protein validation experiments, submit sequences to a cloud lab API, monitor assay status, and interpret returned experimental results.
skill.summary: Plan, submit, and track Adaptyv protein testing experiments from AI coding tools.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most high-severity static matches are false positives caused by placeholder API keys, .env guidance, Markdown fences, or scientific sequence terminology. The real risks are intended outbound API calls to Adaptyv and NetSolP, local example file writes, and disclosure of proprietary protein sequences to a third-party lab service.

remediation.issue: Users may submit confidential protein sequences to third-party services.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear consent warning before examples that send sequences to Adaptyv or NetSolP, and advise users to confirm data-sharing permissions.

remediation.issue: Example file writes use caller-controlled paths or API-derived names.
remediation.suggestion: Normalize output paths in examples, write under an explicit results directory, and document overwrite behavior.

remediation.issue: API authentication examples rely on local environment files.
remediation.suggestion: Keep placeholder-only examples and add a reminder that .env files must remain outside version control.

content.value_statement: Protein teams need a reliable path from designed sequences to experimental validation. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Adaptyv API setup, experiment submission, status tracking, and result handling.
actual_capabilities: Explains Adaptyv API authentication with environment-based API keys.
Shows how to submit single or batch protein sequences for testing.
Documents binding, expression, thermostability, and enzyme activity experiment types.
Provides examples for checking experiment status and retrieving results.
Summarizes protein optimization workflows using tools such as NetSolP, SoluProt, SolubleMPNN, and ESM.
Describes webhook usage and API error handling for long-running experiments.
limitations: Requires an Adaptyv API token and platform access during the alpha or beta period.
Experimental results are not immediate and may take about 21 days.
Some platform features may not be available through the API.
Users must verify permission before sending confidential sequence data to external services.

use_cases.title: Validate designed binders
use_cases.description: Prepare sequence payloads, select a binding assay, and submit variants for experimental testing through Adaptyv.

use_cases.title: Automate experiment tracking
use_cases.description: Build scripts that submit experiments, check status, handle failures, and retrieve completed result summaries.

use_cases.title: Prioritize expression candidates
use_cases.description: Use computational solubility and sequence checks before sending the strongest candidates for wet-lab validation.

prompt_templates.title: Set up authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set up Adaptyv API authentication safely. I have an API token and want to use environment variables.

prompt_templates.title: Submit a single experiment
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a safe plan to submit one protein sequence to Adaptyv for expression testing. Include required fields and data-sharing checks.

prompt_templates.title: Track experiment results
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a workflow that checks an Adaptyv experiment status, handles common API errors, and saves the final result summary locally.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize and validate a library
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prioritize a protein variant library using solubility and naturalness checks, then prepare the top candidates for Adaptyv validation.

output_examples.input: I want to test 20 antibody-like variants for binding.
output_examples.output: The skill would outline a batch submission plan, required target information, metadata fields, and consent checks before sending sequences.

output_examples.input: My experiment is complete. What should I retrieve?
output: Key measurement fields such as affinity or expression level
Quality metrics and links to downloadable reports

output_examples.input: Which variants should I submit first?
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend pre-screening for solubility, sequence validity, and functional residue preservation before selecting candidates.

best_practices: Confirm that sequence data can be shared before submitting it to any external service.
Store API keys in environment variables and keep local credential files out of version control.
Use batch submissions, webhooks, and local validation to reduce failed or duplicate experiments.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real API keys into prompts, code snippets, or shared documents.
Do not submit proprietary sequences without approval from the data owner.
Do not rely on computational scores alone when experimental validation is required.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps plan and automate Adaptyv protein testing workflows, including submission, tracking, and result retrieval.

faq.question: Do I need an Adaptyv account?
faq.answer: Yes. The API examples require an Adaptyv API token and platform access.

faq.question: Can it run experiments by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and API examples. Actual experiments require valid credentials, available credits, and user approval.

faq.question: Is it safe for confidential protein sequences?
faq.answer: Use caution. The workflow sends sequence data to external services, so confirm permission before submission.

faq.question: Which experiment types are covered?
faq.answer: The documentation covers binding assays, expression testing, thermostability measurements, and enzyme activity assays.

faq.question: Can it help optimize sequences before testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes screening and optimization workflows using solubility, structure, and sequence likelihood tools.
